platforms.title: 17 launchpads. One honest coach.
platforms.sub: Fiverr and Upwork are just the start — pick any of these remote-work sites and Atlas coaches you for that site specifically.
platforms.algoNote: Every site plays by its own rules: its own algorithm, its own way of handing out the first order or interview, its own pace. What works on Fiverr flops on a job board. Pick where you want to start — your roadmap and coaching bend to that site, with the patience it demands built in.
platforms.marketplacesHint: buyers come to you — fastest first dollar
platforms.jobBoardsHint: you apply to posted roles with a CV

fiverr.tagline: You publish services (gigs) and buyers come to you — no CV, no interviews. The fastest realistic path to a first dollar.
fiverr.approach: Fiverr ranks gigs like a search engine ranks pages: title keywords, gallery quality, response speed, and early reviews decide who gets seen. New sellers get a visibility window — a complete, specific gig makes it count.
fiverr.patience: A first order typically takes 2–6 weeks of daily showing up, and Fiverr keeps 20% of everything. Nobody honest promises faster.

upwork.tagline: You send proposals to posted jobs — more effort per client, but bigger and longer projects than gig sites.
upwork.approach: A specialized profile and a first line that answers the client's actual problem win here. Proposal credits (Connects) are limited — spend them on fresh posts with few applicants, and let small early jobs build your Job Success Score.
upwork.patience: Expect dozens of tailored proposals before the first win; 4–8 weeks is normal. Copy-paste proposals get you suspended, not hired.

wellfound.tagline: Over 130k startup jobs, from young companies to fast-growing ones — with salary and equity shown before you apply.
wellfound.approach: One profile powers every application, and you often talk directly to founders. Your headline and projects do the selling; a short, specific note beats any formal cover letter.
wellfound.patience: Startup roles lean toward experience and replies take weeks. Best after you have a project or two to show — even spec work counts.

working_nomads.tagline: A curated list of remote jobs for people who work from anywhere, sorted into clear categories.
working_nomads.approach: It is an aggregator: you apply on each company's own site. Turn on the email digest, filter to worldwide-eligible roles, and apply while postings are fresh.
working_nomads.patience: Expect a few good matches a week, not a flood. Fifteen focused minutes a day beats a Sunday binge.

web3_career.tagline: The niche board for blockchain and Web3 companies — developers, but also marketing, design, and community roles.
web3_career.approach: Niche means less competition: learn the Web3 vocabulary and show it. Community moderation is a real entry door. Many posts show salary ranges — use them to set expectations.
web3_career.patience: Scams ride alongside real jobs here: anyone asking you to pay, connect a wallet, or buy tokens is not an employer. Walk away.

remoteok.tagline: One of the biggest open feeds of remote jobs — developer, designer, copywriter, support, and more. No account needed to browse.
remoteok.approach: Newest posts sit on top and the whole world is applying. Check the location tag first — Worldwide only — then apply fast on the company's own form with a tidy CV and short note.
remoteok.patience: Global competition is fierce. Five tailored applications beat fifty copy-pasted ones, every single week.

weworkremotely.tagline: One of the largest remote-work communities in the world, with categories from programming to customer support.
weworkremotely.approach: Employers pay to post, so listings are serious — and crowded. Follow each post's application instructions to the letter; many hide small attention tests. Customer support is the most realistic beginner door.
weworkremotely.patience: Popular posts draw hundreds of applicants. Expect weeks of silence — keep applying while you wait.

jobspresso.tagline: Expertly curated remote jobs in tech, marketing, and customer support — every post reviewed by a human.
jobspresso.approach: Apply to listings, but also upload your resume so employers can find you. Fewer posts, better quality — checking twice a week is the right rhythm.
jobspresso.patience: A quiet board rewards patience. Treat it as one steady stop in your weekly rotation, not a daily jackpot.

flexjobs.tagline: Hand-screened remote, hybrid, and flexible jobs — every listing verified, no scams.
flexjobs.approach: Full access needs a paid membership. In return you get part-time and flexible roles most boards skip — admin, virtual assistance, data entry, support — the categories beginners actually win.
flexjobs.patience: Do the math in taka before subscribing, and join only when you can apply several hours a week. Use it seriously for a month or two, or not at all.

justremote.tagline: Fully and partially remote jobs across development, marketing, design, and HR — filterable by country.
justremote.approach: Set the Anywhere filter first so you never waste time on roles you cannot get. The paid PowerSearch reveals unadvertised roles — optional, and only worth it later.
justremote.patience: A smaller, tidy board. One stop on your weekly checklist, not your only source.

jobgether.tagline: Over 100k remote jobs matched to your profile, each scored for how well it fits you.
jobgether.approach: The profile is the engine: complete skills, languages, time zone, and expectations, then chase only high-match roles. Postings spell out the work setup — check the hours fit your time zone.
jobgether.patience: Mass-applying to low-match roles goes nowhere. Let the match score focus your effort and show you which skill to build next.

underdog.tagline: One application puts you in front of many vetted startups hiring in NYC, SF, and remote.
underdog.approach: The flow is reversed: fill one careful form and interested companies contact you. Every field — especially projects and links — is your whole pitch.
underdog.patience: The US startup bar is high; this is a hard door for absolute beginners. Bank a real project first, then come back.

builtin.tagline: Tech jobs, company profiles, salaries, and news — a research library that happens to list jobs.
builtin.approach: Use it twice: find the role, then read the company profile and culture pages so your cover letter names specifics no template can.
builtin.patience: Roles skew senior and many remote posts are US-only. Read the eligibility line before you invest a minute.

remote_co.tagline: Remote jobs alongside straight answers from real remote companies about how they hire and work.
remote_co.approach: Read the Q&A resources before interviews — knowing async-communication norms is what sets a beginner apart. Support, VA, and data entry are the starter categories.
remote_co.patience: It is part of the FlexJobs family, so some paths lead to a subscription. Work the free portions first.

skipthedrive.tagline: Thousands of remote and hybrid jobs gathered in one simple, no-account-needed place.
skipthedrive.approach: A quick-scan board: skim every day or two, shortlist matches, then apply on the employer's own site.
skipthedrive.patience: Listings lean US and eligibility varies — confirm each post. A supporting source, not the main bet.

remotive.tagline: Tech-focused remote jobs with a newsletter, a community — and region tags on every post.
remotive.approach: Start every search from the Worldwide tag so ineligible roles never cost you a minute. Support and QA are the writing-heavy, non-coding doors in.
remotive.patience: Even with perfect targeting, replies take weeks. The newsletter keeps fresh posts coming to you — apply early.

virtualvocations.tagline: A job service of hand-screened remote leads — every listing checked before it goes up.
virtualvocations.approach: Some listings are free to view; the full database needs a subscription. Strongest in admin, virtual assistant, data entry, and support work.
virtualvocations.patience: Many roles require US residency — hunt specifically for internationally open ones and confirm before applying.
